brevis, breve

adjective, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

short, brief

Short in time and brief in speech (brevis esse, “to be brief”). Brevī is “shortly, soon”, and breviter “briefly”.

Other words

  • breviter — briefly, in a few words

    adverb · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.7.1: quam dulcis sit lībertās, breviter prōloquar; Traupman 283

    The adverb of brevis: of speaking, in few words; of time, for a short while.

  • paulisper — for a short while, for a little while

    also used · classical · Plaut. As. 5.2.30: paulisper manē (Lewis & Short s.v. paulisper); Cic. Verr. 2.4.39: abesse ā domō paulisper māluit (Lewis & Short s.v. ab)

    How long something lasts: a little while (see moment).

  • brevī tempore — given for “for a short time”

    avoid · classical · Traupman 88: for a short time, brevī tempore; Traupman 394

    “In a short time, shortly” (see soon): it says how soon, not how long. For “for a short time”, paulisper (above).

Examples

  • omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt

    anything short ought to be bearable, even if it is greatCic. Amic. 104

  • quidquid praecipiēs, estō brevis

    whatever you teach, be briefHor. Ars 335

  • Brevī redībō.

    I’ll be back shortly.composed

  • Sapiēns quod petitur ubi tacet, breviter negat.

    when a wise man says nothing to a request, he is saying no in shortPubl. S 32

See also short, long, a little later, soon.
